title: 60-Day US-Iran MOU Deadline Expires as Iran Declares Shift to 'Fully Offensive' Policy; IRGC Calls Trump Backchannel Claim 'Lies'
detail: The 60-day memorandum of understanding signed June 18 between the US and Iran expired Aug 17 with no deal reached and no extension announced. Trump told reporters he was 'not in a hurry' and said 'No' when asked if the MOU would be extended. Iran Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei downplayed the deadline, saying Iran 'did not commence negotiations because the United States began violating the memorandum shortly after its June 18 signing.' A senior Iranian official separately told Reuters that Iran has decided to shift its posture from defensive to 'fully offensive,' warning Iranian forces 'must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region' and signaling readiness for a 'timely and precise' military attack to break the US naval blockade if diplomacy fails. The dispute centers on Point 5 of the MOU: Tehran says it grants Iran management rights over the strait; Washington rejects that reading. Separately, IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohibbi flatly denied Trump's claim of a direct US-IRGC backchannel, calling it 'lies' and 'fantasies born of delusions and nightmares resulting from defeat and desperation in the war,' while White House envoy Jared Kushner insisted US-Iran communications are 'more robust' than ever and accused Tehran of trying to 'trick' Washington with false concessions.

media.caption: The Strait of Hormuz remains the central flashpoint as the 60-day US-Iran MOU deadline expires

title: Trump Threatens to 'Bomb the S*** Out of' Oman, Posts Map Claiming Strait of Hormuz as US Territory
detail: In a phone interview with Fox News' Trey Yingst, Trump threatened Oman over its Hormuz diplomacy with Iran: 'If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the s*** out of them,' adding 'we'd handle them very easily, just like we do other things.' The threat came as Iran announced it had reached an agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the strait — coordinates for inbound/outbound lanes, a joint coordination center, and security arrangements — with the two countries finalizing a joint statement, though Iran's FM Araghchi said reopening the strait remained 'subject to other conditions' including US compliance with the MOU. Trump separately posted a social media map depicting the Strait of Hormuz as 'new' US territory, reiterating 'we control it... I like the idea of declaring it a territory.' Iran's Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed the map as a 'delusion' that Iran would 'correct' if the US did not. Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) said he would introduce a Senate resolution barring military action against Oman when the chamber returns from recess.

media.caption: Trump threatens to bomb Oman as Iran announces a Strait of Hormuz shipping deal with Muscat

title: Iranian-Launched Drones Target Kurdistan PM Barzani's Office and Intelligence Chief's Home in Erbil
detail: Two Hadid-110 kamikaze drones struck near the private office of Iraqi Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) Prime Minister Masrour Barzani in Erbil's Pirmam district and the home of the head of the Parastin intelligence agency shortly after midnight (00:28 local) on Aug 17. The Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Directorate said the drones were launched from Iranian territory; no casualties were reported. Barzani called it 'a dangerous escalation and a direct threat to the security and stability of the Kurdistan Region.' Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied Iranian responsibility, saying 'nothing justifies the reckless attack on PM Barzani's office' and urging Kurdish officials to 'be vigilant against false-flag ploys to sow discord between neighbours' — leaving attribution contested between Kurdish security's territorial tracing and Iran's denial. Iraqi PM Ali Faleh al-Zaidi ordered an investigative committee. The strike was the latest in a wave of at least 16 drones and 3 missiles that hit Iraqi Kurdistan in the first two weeks of August.

media.caption: Drones targeted KRG PM Masrour Barzani's office and the Parastin intelligence chief's home in Erbil

confidenceReason: Kurdish Counter-Terrorism Directorate traced launch to Iranian territory and identified Iranian-made Hadid-110 drones, but Iran's Foreign Ministry denies responsibility and suggests a false-flag operation; no independent confirmation of attribution.

title: Houthis Claim Ballistic Missile Strikes 'Completely Burned' Saudi Military Landing Ship in Red Sea
detail: Yemen's Houthi movement said it targeted a Saudi military landing ship and four escorting patrol boats off the coast of Mokha in the Red Sea, part of the maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia the group declared July 20. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said fighters used 'several ballistic missiles' against the vessels, claiming the landing ship was 'completely burned' and several escort boats sunk or set alight. Saudi Arabia did not confirm the claims and there was no independent verification. The attack follows the collapse of the UN-backed 2022 Red Sea truce after a Saudi airstrike on Sanaa airport's runway on Jul 13 prevented an Iranian delegation's flight from landing.

media.caption: Houthi forces claim a ballistic missile strike on a Saudi military landing ship off Mokha, Red Sea

confidenceReason: Single-source Houthi claim (spokesperson Yahya Saree); Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attack or the claimed damage.

title: Pentagon Awards Raytheon $22.9 Billion Contract to Boost Tomahawk Missile Production 17-Fold
detail: The US Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion, seven-year contract to ramp up production of Tomahawk cruise missiles from roughly 60 per year to more than 1,000 per year, formalizing a framework agreement signed in February. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the deal 'ensures our warfighters continue to have the lethal firepower they need' and will accelerate missile delivery at 'unprecedented speed.' The contract reflects Pentagon concern over depleted precision-munitions stockpiles after sustained Tomahawk use in the Iran campaign alongside continued arms transfers to allies.
